one_liner: Hand-written AVX-512F SGEMM/DGEMM with a Fortran-ABI entry point; claims 99% of one-thread MKL, which is parity, not a win.
what_it_does: The Makefile builds SGEMM.so and DGEMM.so, each exporting a Fortran-ABI sgemm_ or dgemm_ (transa, transb, m, n, k, alpha, A, lda, B, ldb, beta, C, ldc, with 32-bit int arguments, column-major), so it can stand in for the GEMM symbol of an LP64 BLAS. It provides GEMM only, with no cblas_ interface and no other BLAS routines. A separate OpenBLAS-like_implementation/ directory holds the author's OpenBLAS-format SkylakeX kernels (dgemm 16x2 and 4x8, cgemm3m and zgemm3m, a dtrsm 16x4 solver, and a serial stand-alone sgemm.c with its own SGEMM_ test caller).
how_it_is_fast: It uses Goto-style blocking. Each thread packs its own B block, with alpha folded into the packed copy. A is packed once per K block into a buffer that all threads share. A GNU-assembler micro-kernel (src/kernel/gemm_kernel.S) keeps GEMM_UNROLL_M_VEC x GEMM_UNROLL_N zmm accumulators live, by default 3x8 = 24 registers (a 48x8 tile for SGEMM, 24x8 for DGEMM), and updates them with vbroadcastss/sd plus vfmadd231ps/pd. The software-prefetch distances (prefetcht0/t1) into packed A and B come from the L2/L3 latency and FMA-unit parameters in sgemm_tune.h and dgemm_tune.h, and AVX512_CPUTEST.c measures FMA throughput and latency to help set them. Threads split N into equal column chunks and meet at a spin barrier around each shared A pack.
when_to_use: Reading a complete, small AVX-512 GEMM (assembly micro-kernel, packing, prefetch-distance arithmetic, OpenMP driver) in under 2,000 lines.
Experimenting with register-tile and cache-block parameters on an AVX-512 Xeon: change the tune headers, rebuild, and compare against your own MKL or OpenBLAS runs.
A GPL-3.0-compatible project that wants a self-contained sgemm_/dgemm_ without a full BLAS and accepts roughly MKL single-thread speed as the best case.
Tracing where OpenBLAS's SkylakeX DGEMM and STRMM kernels came from (the author committed them upstream in 2020).
when_not_to_use: If you want to beat MKL or OpenBLAS: the only claim is 99% of one-thread MKL, with no numbers, sizes, CPU or MKL version, and the repo has no GEMM benchmark program.
CPUs without AVX-512F, or non-ELF platforms: the kernels are System V AMD64 assembly (.type @function, stack red zone), so Windows and macOS builds are not supported as written.

Multi-threaded production use: thread 0 packs A alone while the others spin, and the one issue (#1, 2020) reports that the OpenMP .so is less efficient than the serial sgemm.c. Plain OpenBLAS already contains the author's upstreamed kernels and is maintained.
Anything that needs maintenance or other BLAS routines: last commit 2022-05-22, GEMM only, no tests and no argument checking.

integration.min_toolchain: GCC with -mavx512f and the GNU assembler (AT&T-syntax .S); C11 aligned_alloc; exact GCC version not documented
integration.platforms: x86-64 with AVX-512F, ELF / System V ABI (Linux); default parameters tuned on a Xeon Platinum 8269CY
integration.thread_safety: Each call allocates its own buffers, so separate calls share no state. However, each call opens an OpenMP team sized by omp_get_max_threads() and spin-waits until every thread arrives, so a call from inside another OpenMP parallel region, or with OMP_DYNAMIC or a thread limit, can hang (inferred from src/gemm_driver.c, not tested).
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: it exports Fortran-ABI sgemm_/dgemm_ with 32-bit integers and can therefore replace the GEMM symbol of an LP64 MKL or OpenBLAS, but it has no cblas_sgemm, no ILP64 and no other routines, and beta=0 does not overwrite C the way the BLAS spec allows.

gotchas: beta=0 multiplies C by zero (C_MULT_BETA) instead of overwriting it, so NaN or Inf already in C survive; reference BLAS lets callers pass an unset C when beta is zero.
The thread count comes from omp_get_max_threads(). For the single-thread setting the 99% claim refers to, set OMP_NUM_THREADS=1.
Tuning is compile-time only, by editing sgemm_tune.h and dgemm_tune.h; gemm_set_parameters.h silently clamps out-of-range values (for example GEMM_UNROLL_N is capped at 24/GEMM_UNROLL_M_VEC).
aligned_alloc and malloc results are not checked, nothing returns early when m, n or k is 0, and the assembly defines a global symbol with the generic name timedelay (used by the spin barrier).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it only to study or retune an AVX-512 GEMM kernel. The same author's GEMM_AVX2_FMA3 at least publishes numbers against MKL 2019 (2-3% faster at 20000^3 on 8 threads), FT-BLAS claims up to 3.5% over MKL, and stock OpenBLAS already ships this author's SkylakeX DGEMM and STRMM kernels.
verified_claims_summary: The only performance statement is the README line 'able to reach 99% MKL 1-thread performance after tuning'. It gives no GFLOPS, matrix sizes, MKL version, compiler or CPU, and the repo contains no GEMM benchmark (AVX512_CPUTEST.c only measures peak FMA throughput and latency); the tune headers say the parameters were tuned on a Xeon Platinum 8269CY. Read literally, it is a 1% deficit against single-threaded MKL: parity, not a win.
status_note: Abandoned since 2022-05-22 (82 commits, 15 stars, one open 2020 issue) and GPL-3.0, so vendoring it brings copyleft. Its lasting value is upstream: the author's OpenBLAS commits include 'AVX512 16x2 DGEMM kernel' (2020-02-03) and 'AVX512 STRMM kernel' (2020-02-16), matching the AVX512 DGEMM kernel added in OpenBLAS 0.3.8 and the SkylakeX STRMM kernel in 0.3.9.
